items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I was doing a recording date with a singer named Shirley Horne. It was a big string date

ctx.x: That's the only thing I can say, he just loved it. In fact the last time I saw him was in New York and I was doing a recording date with a singer named Shirley Horne. It was a big string date, you know, we had about 20 strings or so. And Arnold Wright came to the record date. He was visiting in New York, you know. And he knew of John Levy and John Levy was in the booth producing the date. So Arnold Wright looked at me -- oh, this was years later, a generation
later I guess, and he says, "Whatever happened to that fellow John Levy?" I said, "You've been sitting next to him for the last two hours."

items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jimmy Jones is number-one pianist for me. He‘s the accompanist. I mean, I‘m so comfortable with him.

ctx.x: No, I didn‘t like that. You know, I had my choice of the finest pianists, but I mean like today, nobody knows how to play for me what I can play for me. Jimmy Jones is number-one pianist for me. He‘s the accompanist. I mean, I‘m so comfortable with him. But I ain‘t happy with nobody else.
Was it difficult for you to even be able to sing, I mean, when you were recording those albums, not being able, like, to hear things, where you‘re hearing things that they weren‘t playing?
